subject: Post-demo privacy recap: DPA, SCC module, and controller/processor alignment
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novuspay.com>, NovusPay Procurement <procurement@novuspay.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 09:15:00 -0500
Subject: Post-demo recap and DPA / SCC next steps

Hi Elena — thanks again for joining the demo this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps from our side so procurement and legal have clear items to work from: 

1) DPA & SCC module: please confirm whether NovusPay prefers the standard DPA with the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCC) Module for Controller-to-Processor or if you need Module-to-Module language (we can support either but we need the preference to route the correct DPA draft).

2) Controller/Processor alignment: on the call you said NovusPay will act as the Controller for customer payment data; please confirm that Redwood will be the Processor for any hosted inference and storage. If you have scenarios where NovusPay is acting as Processor (e.g., data residency or specific integrations), flag those and we’ll coordinate the language.

3) SOC 2 / compliance artifacts: could you share the current SOC 2 status (Type I vs Type II, and expected completion if in-flight) and any high-level compliance docs we can attach to the vendor intake?

4) Vendor security questionnaire (VSQ): we’ll kick off our VSQ once we have the right DPA/SCC direction. Please confirm the procurement contact for DocuSign routing and timeline.

Attachments: call-recording-20280112.mp4 (recording), demo-slide-deck.pdf (internal reference).

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm SCC module choice and controller/processor roles (reply here)
- We’ll send a DPA draft aligned with your preference and kick off the VSQ portal link
- Procurement routes contracts to procurement@novuspay.com and copies your legal lead

I’ll loop in David from Legal for the DPA draft and retention/subprocessor questions. Thanks —

Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0198
https://redwood.com
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novuspay.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: NovusPay Procurement <procurement@novuspay.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 11:02:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap and DPA / SCC next steps

Hi Tessa — great demo, thanks. Quick answers below and a couple items attached.

- SCC module: NovusPay requires Controller-to-Processor language. We would expect Redwood to sign as Processor for hosted services.

- Controller/Processor: confirmed — NovusPay will act as Controller for customer payment and PII associated with transactions. Redwood should be Processor for inference, embeddings, and any cached data. If there are features that store customer-owned data longer than 30 days, call that out and we’ll flag for legal.

- SOC 2: we currently maintain SOC 2 Type II (most recent report is for the period ending 2026-11-30). We are preparing a refreshed attestation for Q2 2028; I’ve attached a high-level security overview and a redacted SOC 2 summary.

- Procurement contact: procurement@novuspay.com (cc’d). Procurement prefers contracts routed through DocuSign and expects to complete internal review within 2–3 weeks once the preferred DPA is provided.

I attached: NovusPay_Security_Overview.pdf (summary), procurement-timeline.pdf (procurement notes).

We’re ready for a DPA draft that uses Controller (NovusPay) -> Processor (Redwood) SCC Module language. Once we have the DPA, we’ll have procurement loop in our legal counsel for final review.

Thanks —
Elena Ruiz
Head of Integrations | NovusPay
elena.ruiz@novuspay.com

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, NovusPay Procurement <procurement@novuspay.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 12:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap and DPA / SCC next steps

Hi Elena — appreciate the quick reply and the attachments. A few legal/ops clarifications so we draft the correct DPA: 

1) Processor responsibilities: Redwood will be listed as Processor for hosted inference and operational logs. Could you confirm maximum retention expectations for logs/embeddings (NovusPay preference — e.g., 30 days, 90 days, or custom retention per customer)? If any endpoints will require longer retention, please enumerate them.

2) Subprocessors: we maintain a subprocessor list and will include standard cloud infra providers. Procurement: we’ll share the current subprocessor registry in the DPA. Any NovaPay-specific disallowed subprocessors?

3) Cross-border transfer mechanism: since you selected Controller->Processor SCC language, we’ll include the EU SCC Module appropriate for that mapping. If NovusPay has a specific SCC variant or bespoke data transfer clause, flag now.

4) VSQ: we’ve provisioned a VSQ instance for NovusPay to complete: https://redwoodsecurity.com/vsq/novuspay-123. Please ask your security team to start the questionnaire; it syncs directly to our intake and speeds procurement.

I’ve attached a starter DPA draft (DPA_draft_Redwood_v1.docx) with our standard Processor terms and a short retention table placeholder — please have your legal team mark any changes.

Would be helpful if procurement could target Feb 1 for an executed DPA so we can start integration during your Q1 onboarding window.

Thanks —
David Kim
Legal Ops | Redwood Inference
D: (415) 555-0123

Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 14:10:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap and DPA / SCC next steps

Thanks David — confirmed answers from procurement and legal below: 

- Retention: default retention for logs and embeddings is 30 days. We have a standard exception process for longer retention tied to signed customer SLAs — if you need a retention table in the DPA we’ll provide an example SLA clause.

- Subprocessors: procurement flagged that AWS and FastCDN are allowed subprocessors; NovusPay has no additional disallowed subprocessors. You can include the standard registry.

- SCC variant: Controller-to-Processor SCC Module is fine; no bespoke clauses required at this stage.

Procurement note: they’ll accept a draft DPA and route via DocuSign. Expect a 10–15 business day review once the draft is provided. Procurement contact for final signature is procurement@novuspay.com.

I’m attaching a redacted purchase-order-template.pdf for your procurement ops to review (attached as procurement-timeline.pdf).

Next steps (agreed):
- Redwood to send DPA draft with Controller->Processor SCC module + retention table placeholder (David)
- NovusPay security to start VSQ: https://redwoodsecurity.com/vsq/novuspay-123
- Procurement to route via DocuSign to procurement@novuspay.com once draft is ready

Happy to jump on a short call if you want to walk through the DPA draft after you send it.

Best —
Elena Ruiz
Head of Integrations | NovusPay
